## Company Overview

**Sources:** the 9-page website crawl and the website positioning notes. No live web access. The company profile says what Acme Advisory sells and who its competitors are is "Not provided", so the product details below come from the website only.

### Brand & Positioning

- **Name and mark:** Acme Advisory (the degree sign appears in page titles and the logo).
- **Homepage headline:** "Human Intelligence in the age of AI".
- **Homepage promise:** "We help product and revenue leaders define and execute their product, growth, and AI transformation strategy."
- **Browser title:** "Human Intelligence for AI-Enabled Product & Revenue Leaders". It names the audience more clearly than the H1.
- **What it is:** a one-founder advisory, tools and workshops business focused on AI adoption. The site menu splits it into three parts.
  - **Advisory:**
    - Product management for SaaS founders.
    - Product-led growth and go-to-market strategy for revenue leaders.
    - AI transformation for small and medium businesses.
  - **Products** (the homepage says "Tools built from real engagements"):
    - **10x Employee:** a company "Brain" in plain files plus AI agents, for faster onboarding. DIY is free. White-glove is custom priced. Build runs about 8 weeks.
    - **Private AI:** open-weight models on a dedicated computer in the office, for regulated firms of roughly 3 to 25 people. Takes about two months. Price not shown.
    - **AI Chief of Staff:** free, open source, 8 commands, runs in Claude.
    - **AI Use Policy Generator:** free, open source. Seven questions produce six documents.
    - **PositioningHQ:** free, open source Claude skills that build a 7-part positioning playbook, battlecards and call plans. The homepage card calls it "Sales Enablement Automation". The page itself is titled "PositioningHQ".
  - **Workshops:**
    - **AI Accelerator:** a 2-day offsite, 8 seats, in Vancouver (boardroom) or Whistler (retreat, December 5 to 6). Price "to be announced". Check-ins at 30, 60 and 90 days.
    - **Executive AI Fluency:** 3 live 90-minute sessions where you build your own AI chief of staff.
- **Main differentiator claimed:** operator credibility. "Hands-on advice from someone who has run the function."
- **Tone:** plain, direct, practical, confident. Example: "Stop asking AI questions. Start working with it."
- **Proof on the site:**
  - Founder career credentials.
  - Two named testimonials: Laurie Schultz (Board Director, Serial Chair, Investor, Technology CEO) and Reza Varzidehkar (CEO, OVOU).
  - One anonymous workshop anecdote about a CEO using the tool during a product recall.
  - No customer logos, case studies, results or awards.
- **Positioning issues visible from the site:**
  - **No single category.** Advisory, free tools and workshops sit side by side with no one lead offer.
  - **Audience mismatch.** The homepage speaks to product and revenue leaders. Most product pages speak to CEOs, founders, owners and regulated professional firms. Only PositioningHQ (reps) and the advisory menu match the homepage audience.
  - **No visible primary call to action on the homepage.** It has five "See how it works" links. A "Book a call" link (cal.com/acme-advisory/intro) appears in the header on the page where it was captured.
  - **Product naming is inconsistent.** One product is called "Sales Enablement Automation" on the homepage and "PositioningHQ" on its own page.
  - **Thin proof.** No measurable customer outcomes.
  - **Unrecorded sections.** The "How we know it works" and "Questions" sections were captured as headings only.

### History

- **Founding date and story:** Not available. The site has no founding story, and the crawl found no dated company history. The footer reads "© 2026 Acme Advisory".
- **Founder:** Sam Rivera (named in the profile as Sam, Founder or CEO).
  - 25 years building business software companies.
  - VP of Product at Galvanize. He "helped scale the company to a $1B exit".
  - Chief Product & Technology Officer at Boast AI. He "led the move to AI in how the company built and delivered its product".
  - Says he still builds AI agents himself.
- **Co-host:** Atta Emami appears on the AI Accelerator page. The site gives no formal role or relationship to Acme Advisory beyond hosting.
  - 20+ years in leadership and change work.
  - 6.5 years at Shopify coaching senior leaders.
  - Led large-scale change at AIG across Asia Pacific and Latin America, and culture transformation at Central 1 Credit Union.
- **Other channels:** a newsletter at inhouse.build and a LinkedIn company page.
- **Product timeline:** Not available. No launch dates or version history were found.

### Size

- **Employees:** Just the founder, per the company profile. The profile wins over anything on the site. The site's use of "we" and the co-host Atta Emami are not treated as staff.
- **Revenue:** Not available. Nothing is published.
- **Customers:** Not available. The site names two testimonial givers and no customer count.
- **Funding:** Not available.

### HQ

- **Headquarters:** Not stated on the site.
- **Location signals only:**
  - The AI Accelerator boardroom is in downtown Vancouver.
  - The retreat is in Whistler.
  - Executive AI Fluency is delivered remotely.
  - Private AI needs on-site installation, but no service area is given.
- **Inference, not confirmed:** the business is likely based in or near British Columbia, Canada.
- **Contact:** sam@acme-advisory.example

### Mission

- **Stated mission or values:** Not available. No mission statement or values page was found.
- **Implied from the copy (inference):**
  - **Make AI practical for leaders.** Make AI usable by leaders who are expected to lead on it. "It's hard to lead something you don't do yourself."
  - **Own your data.** "Plain files you own", "No database and no account with us", "Take everything with you any time".
  - **Set rules before tools.** Clear rules over blanket bans, with a human reviewing AI output.
  - **Be honest about limits.** Examples: "If you don't need this, we'll tell you." The Private AI page also has a "What it doesn't do" section.
  - **Learn by doing.** "This isn't a course." "You'll learn them by using them."
- **Next step for the wiki:** the founder should confirm or replace these inferred values.

## Product Analysis

**Scope note:** The company profile does not say what Acme Advisory sells. This analysis is built from the public website and linked pages. Pricing, customer counts and usage data are not available. Only the 10x Employee product page was read in full. The other product pages were not reviewed, so their descriptions come from the home page.

### Offerings

**Company shape:** Acme Advisory is a solo advisory practice led by Sam Rivera that also ships productized tools and workshops. The site navigation splits the business into Advisory, Products and Workshops. The home page describes this as "advisory, products and workshops for product, growth and AI."

**1. Advisory (three lines)**
- **Product:** Product management discipline for SaaS startup founders. It covers a clear strategy, an outcome-tied roadmap and evidence that customers will pay before building.
- **Growth:** Product-led growth and go-to-market strategy for revenue leaders. It covers positioning buyers understand, a product that sells itself where it can, a sales team equipped where it can't, and win/loss analysis.
- **AI:** AI transformation for small and medium businesses.

**2. Products ("tools built from real engagements")**

| Product | What it is | Price signal |
|---|---|---|
| 10x Employee | An AI operating system that amplifies every employee. | Free do-it-yourself playbook and plugin, or white-glove service at custom pricing. |
| Private AI | AI that runs inside your office, so client data stays there. | Not available |
| AI Chief of Staff | Marked Free. It knows your priorities, projects and people, and opens every session with a brief. | Free |
| AI Use Policy Generator | Marked Free. Answer a few questions to get a one-page AI use policy, approved tools list, vendor checklist and team rollout. | Free |
| Sales Enablement Automation | Turns your positioning into a playbook, battlecards and call plans reps will use. | Not available on the home page |

**3. Workshops**
- **AI Accelerator:** Two days for CEOs and founders. Attendees leave with a practical AI roadmap built with peers and two guides. It runs by application, with dates to be announced.
- **Executive AI Fluency:** Three hands-on sessions for leadership teams. Each leader builds an AI chief of staff and second brain.

**4. PositioningHQ (related offering)**
- PositioningHQ is described as a Acme Advisory offering.
- It is run as a workshop. Its page is titled "The Positioning Playbook Workshop for Revenue Teams" and the headline is about winning more deals with Claude and a positioning playbook.
- One listing shows a Maven cohort format.
- The home page links "Sales Enablement Automation" to the `/positioninghq/` path, so the two appear to be the same offering. This is an inference.

**5. Newsletter:** A newsletter sits at inhouse.build. Content and cadence were not reviewed.

### Key Features

**10x Employee (the only product page reviewed in full)**
- **Company "Brain":** Business knowledge lives in plain files the customer owns, as markdown in GitHub, split into everyone, department, private and shared skills.
- **Per-hire AI agent:** Every new hire gets an agent that already knows the business. The pitch is "useful in week two, not month four."
- **Daily brief and update:** A brief lists meetings with context, open promises and an agenda. The daily team update is drafted from short answers.
- **Sourced answers:** Answers show the approved source. If nobody wrote it down, the agent says so and names who to ask.
- **Human-approved learning:** Agents can suggest additions to the Brain, and a person approves them.
- **Access guardrails:** Each agent sees only what its person can see, and nothing leaves the company without a person.
- **Delivery model:** An eight-week program: design in week 1, build in weeks 2 to 5, train in weeks 6 to 7, hand over in week 8.
- **Acceptance test:** The "Day-One Test": a newcomer is set up within an hour, and their agent correctly answers ten typical new-hire questions.
- **Target buyers:** Small business owners, CEOs of growing companies and startup founders.

**Other products:** Feature detail is limited to the one-line descriptions in the table above. Detailed features for Private AI and the other tools are not available.

### Tech Stack

- **Model-agnostic design (10x Employee):** Each job runs on whichever AI model does it best or cheapest, and all read the same Brain. Changing models loses nothing.
- **Illustrative model mix on the page:**
  - Grok agents on xAI's cloud for the daily brief, check-in update and meeting coordination.
  - Claude agents on Anthropic's cloud for onboarding, Ask and Teach the Brain, and the sales kit.
  - Open-weights agents on the customer's own server for meeting notes and the weekly digest, with no per-use fees.
  - The page labels this as illustrative. Models are picked with the customer in week one.
- **Storage and delivery:** Plain markdown in GitHub. The do-it-yourself option is delivered as a playbook and a plugin.
- **Integrations:** The onboarding skill connects email, calendar, the Brain and a private password vault.
- **PositioningHQ:** Built around Claude. The methodology draws on April Dunford's positioning principles and Jobs to Be Done, with an AI layer added.
- **Site tooling:** Google Tag Manager is present. Booking runs through cal.com.
- **Not available:** The website's own framework and hosting, plus any proprietary code beyond the plugin and playbook.

### Evolution

Dates are not published. The evidence below is a snapshot comparison, not a dated timeline.

- **Earlier positioning (search snippet of the same domain):**
  - "AI consulting practice helping executives and their organizations lead AI transformation."
  - Three disciplines: AI transformation and change leadership, AI sales enablement and automation, and AI compliance and ISO 42001.
  - The headline was "Define Your North."
  - The "3 practice disciplines" were listed as AI Sales Enablement, AI Governance and AI Chief of Staff.
- **Current positioning (fetched page):**
  - The page title is "Human Intelligence for AI-Enabled Product & Revenue Leaders."
  - The framing is the "build trap": AI has lowered the cost of building and raised the risk of building the wrong thing.
  - The structure moved from a governance-led consultancy to advisory plus products plus workshops.
  - ISO 42001 is not mentioned in the fetched page text. ISO 42001 certification appeared on the earlier version.
- **Shifts observed:**
  - The audience widened from executives to product founders, revenue leaders and SMB owners.
  - Reusable products appeared ("tools built from real engagements"), with several marked Free.
  - Workshops were added.
  - The founder's own writing points to the market thesis. A May 2026 LinkedIn post says mid-market executives are cancelling SaaS subscriptions and building AI capabilities in-house.
- **Founder background used as proof:** 25 years building business software companies, VP of Product at Galvanize through a $1B exit, and Chief Product & Technology Officer at Boast AI. The home page says 25 years. Older and other pages say 20 years, and this inconsistency is worth fixing. The company profile gives the founder as Sam.
- **Not available:** Launch dates, version history and retired offerings.

### UVP

**Stated value proposition:** "Hands-on advice from someone who has run the function." The company helps build "solutions that sell and stick."

**What appears distinctive (analyst view):**
1. **Operator-led, solo practice.** Advice comes from a former product executive who "still builds AI agents himself."
2. **Tools born from client work, often free.** This lowers the barrier to trying the practice and doubles as lead generation.
3. **Owned, model-agnostic architecture.** The customer owns the plain-file Brain, and models can be swapped without lock-in. This is the strongest technical differentiator on the pages reviewed.
4. **Privacy and governance as design principles.** Examples are Private AI, access-scoped agents, human approval and an audit trail.
5. **Positioning and sales enablement depth.** This comes from PositioningHQ and the "Growth" advisory line. It is the area closest to the founder's goals for this wiki.

**Gaps and risks to resolve in the positioning work:**
- **Too many offers.** The site lists three advisory lines, five products and two workshops, all run by one person. There is no single clear "what we sell" in the profile either.
- **Inconsistent audience and claims.** Audiences include founders, revenue leaders, SMBs and executives. Founder tenure is stated as both 25 and 20 years.
- **No proof points.** The pages reviewed show no named customers, results or pricing, and none of the 10x Employee FAQ answers are visible.
- **Crowded category.** Open-source AI chief-of-staff projects and product directories already exist. GitHub lists public AI chief-of-staff repositories built on Claude Code and Obsidian. Product Hunt has an AI Chief of Staff category. A free chief-of-staff tool is unlikely to differentiate on its own.

**Assumptions:** The current website text is treated as the company's own description of its offerings. No named competitors were provided, so none are analysed here.

## Market Segment

**Assumptions:** The company profile has no product description or named competitors. Acme Advisory's own website describes it as an AI consulting practice helping executives and their organizations lead AI transformation. I used that to define the segment. Third-party market figures are analyst estimates and vary widely. Source quality is mixed, and several sources are vendor blogs.

### Industry

- **Primary industry:** AI consulting and advisory services. This sits inside management and IT consulting.
- **Sub-sectors Acme Advisory claims (from its website):**
  - AI Transformation & Change Leadership: strategy, governance and organizational change.
  - AI Sales Enablement & Automation: AI for sales and marketing teams.
  - AI Compliance & ISO 42001: AI governance and certification support.
- **Delivery model:** Sam Rivera helps executives lead their organization's AI transformation. This is a solo, founder-led practice (profile: "Just me").
- **Adjacent categories:**
  - AI governance software and platforms. These are products, not services.
  - ISO 42001 advisory and audit services. One report says ISO 42001 certification is generating a secondary market in advisory and audit services.
- **Buyer segmentation used by analysts:** Reports split the market by enterprise size (small and mid-sized vs large enterprise). They also split it by end-user vertical. Acme Advisory's site does not name a target size or vertical. That is a positioning gap.

### Position

- **Classification:** Emerging niche player. This is my assessment, not a sourced fact.
  - It is a one-person practice, so it has no scale or market share in a market led by global firms.
  - The website does not list case studies, named clients or a team in the retrieved snippet. Not available for review beyond the snippet.
- **Where the market is led:**
  - Tier 1 strategy houses and Big Four firms dominate the large-enterprise tier. One ranking lists McKinsey QuantumBlack, BCG X and Bain Vector for strategy, and Deloitte AI, EY.ai, KPMG Lighthouse and PwC AI for Big-4 governance.
- **Where a solo practice can credibly play:**
  - Advisors suggest matching firm type to the buyer's constraint. Strategy gaps point to MBB and Big Four. Build gaps point to boutiques, dev shops or a fractional team.
  - Acme Advisory is strategy, governance and change. That puts it in the strategy lane, against the biggest brands. It needs a sharper wedge than "AI strategy for executives".
- **Possible wedges visible in its own copy:**
  - The ISO 42001 certification path.
  - AI for sales and marketing teams, including competitive intelligence.
  - The "Define Your North" and 79°N Svalbard brand idea.
  - Which wedge to lead with is a decision for the next steps.

### Size

**TAM: global AI consulting services.** Estimates differ by source and definition. No single figure is authoritative.

| Source | 2025 value | Forecast | CAGR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wiseguy Reports | $5.16B in 2025, $25B by 2035 | 2035 | about 17.1% |
| The Business Research Company | $7.39B in 2025, $19.47B by 2030 | 2030 | 21.4% |
| Fortune Business Insights | $9.65B in 2025 | $73.89B by 2034 | 25.6% |
| Future Market Insights | $11.07B in 2025, $90.99B by 2035 | 2035 | 23.4% |
| Business Research Insights | $11.13B in 2025, $116.81B by 2034 | 2034 | 26.49% |

- **Range:** roughly $5B to $11B in 2025. Growth forecasts run from about 17% to 26.5% a year. One roundup concludes the market is growing between 20 and 26% annually.
- **Region:** North America held a 38.13% share in 2025. Applied to Fortune's $9.65B, that is about $3.7B. This is my own arithmetic.

**Adjacent market: AI governance.** This is mostly software, so it is an upper bound for Acme Advisory's governance service line, not a direct TAM.
- Estimates for 2025 range from $309M (Precedence Research) to $353M (IMARC) and $940M (Next Move Strategy Consulting).
- Growth forecasts run from 28.15% a year (Mordor Intelligence, $440M in 2026 to $1.51B by 2031) to 51% a year (Next Move).
- One outlier report puts the 2025 market at $5.9B with 10.9% growth. I treat it as non-comparable because the definition is unclear.

**SAM for Acme Advisory:** Not available. No source sizes executive-level AI strategy, governance and change advisory for solo or boutique providers. The profile gives no target geography, buyer size or pricing, so I did not estimate one. To size it, define the target buyer first (for example, mid-market firms in one region). Then count the firms and multiply by an assumed engagement value.

### Competitors

**Market share data:** Not available. I found no reliable share figures by firm.

**Tier 1: strategy houses.** These win on board-level credibility.
- **McKinsey QuantumBlack:** roughly 1,700 people across 40+ offices.
- **BCG X:** about 3,000 technologists and data scientists combined with BCG's strategy consulting. It also often brings a working demo into the room with the recommendation.
- **Bain Vector:** one ranking calls it the best Tier 1 firm for private-equity-backed AI value creation.
- BCG's "10-20-70" model puts 70% of effort into people and process. This overlaps directly with Acme Advisory's change-leadership message.

**Tier 2: Big Four and global integrators.** These win on governance, controls and scale.
- Deloitte AI, PwC AI, EY.ai and KPMG Lighthouse.
- Accenture and IBM Consulting. One source says Accenture has the largest GenAI practice.
- Deloitte is positioned for governance and controls. This is the main competitor for the ISO 42001 and compliance offer.

**Tier 3: boutiques and specialists.** These are the closest peers.
- Examples named in sources: AY Automate, LeewayHertz, Kanerika, Neurons Lab, Vstorm, Addepto, Tribe AI and deepsense.ai. Most skew toward engineering and building, not executive change leadership.
- A fractional Chief AI Officer is a related model. AY Automate offers hands-on strategy with a fractional Chief AI Officer.
- **Pricing:** The only figures I found come from a vendor comparison blog and should be treated as indicative. It lists day rates of $500-700/hr for McKinsey QuantumBlack and project-based $200K-1M for boutiques. No Acme Advisory pricing was found.

**Alternatives to hiring a consultant:**
- AI governance platforms. IBM announced validation against 12 regulatory frameworks in 2025.
- Internal teams and generic training.
- ISO 42001 certification bodies.

**Named competitors in the profile:** None provided. The set above is inferred from the category. The founder should confirm which ones actually show up in deals.

### Trends

1. **AI spend is high but the value gap is wide.** This is the core of Acme Advisory's message ("Most AI rollouts fail... because the organization wasn't led through the change").
   - A WRITER survey of 2,400 people found 79% of organizations face adoption challenges and 59% invest over $1M a year.
   - The same survey says 75% of executives admit their AI strategy is "more for show".
   - WRITER sells AI software, so treat these figures as vendor data.
   - Gartner (Sept 2026, via a secondary source) reports only 22% of organizations have scaled AI across multiple business units.
   - Be careful with "X% of AI projects fail" claims. Sources measure different things. One analysis calls the failure statistic the most-cited and most-abused in enterprise AI. Cite one primary study with its definition.

2. **People and change are the bottleneck.** This supports the change-leadership positioning.
   - IBM's 2026 CEO study, as cited by a secondary source, found 83% of CEOs say AI success depends more on people's adoption than on the technology.
   - A review of 163 transformation failures found 92% were primarily organizational or operational, not technical. This is a secondary source with a small sample.

3. **Governance lags deployment.**
   - IBM's AI control-gap study (2,000 executives), as summarized by a secondary source, found 67% are held accountable for AI systems they don't fully control.
   - WRITER reports 67% of executives believe their company already suffered a data breach due to unapproved AI tools. This matches the site's line about teams "using tools you haven't reviewed".

4. **Regulation and standards are creating demand.**
   - ISO/IEC 42001 is the first international AI management system standard. Roughly 350 organizations worldwide had certified by mid-2026, per industry compilations, with no official global register. The base is small and early.
   - EU AI Act dates and penalties differ across sources. One lists Article 50 applicability on 2 August 2026. Another cites penalties of up to €35 million or 7% of global turnover for the most serious violations. Verify against the official text before using either in marketing.

5. **Market growth is driven by governance and transformation demand.** One report attributes forecast growth partly to demand for responsible AI and governance frameworks and investment in AI transformation strategies.

6. **Buyers sort providers by constraint, not brand.** Advice to buyers now says the best firm fits your stage, data and talent gap, not the biggest brand. This helps a specialist boutique if it names a specific buyer and problem.

7. **Messaging crowding.** Most competitor pages use generic "AI strategy and transformation" language. Acme Advisory's current headline, "Define Your North", is brand-led and does not state a buyer or outcome. Test this in the competitor and messaging steps.

**Gaps in this research:**
- No Acme Advisory customers, pricing or case studies were found.
- No SAM or share data was found.
- Acme Advisory's full website was only seen as a search snippet.

**Sources:** acme-advisory.example; Fortune Business Insights; Future Market Insights; The Business Research Company; Wiseguy Reports; Business Research Insights; Mordor Intelligence; IMARC; Precedence Research; Next Move Strategy Consulting; NovelVista; Dialectica; WRITER; Gartner and IBM (via secondary sources); agent.nexus; Alice Labs; AY Automate; Iternal.

## Customer Segment

**Evidence note:** Acme Advisory's site pages are the main source, and the profile gives no customer data. The site shows two versions of its positioning. The search snippet describes executive AI strategy, governance and ISO 42001. The live homepage describes advisory, products and workshops for product, growth and AI. I treated the live homepage as current. No customer list, case studies or testimonials were found.

### Profiles

- **Primary buyer, advisory:** Product and revenue leaders defining and executing product, growth and AI transformation strategy.
- **Three advisory buyer sub-profiles:**
  - SaaS startup founders who need a product practice the team can run without them.
  - Revenue leaders who need positioning buyers understand, plus a sales team that is equipped.
  - Small and medium businesses pursuing AI transformation.
- **Executive teams on AI:** Sam advises executive teams on where to start, what to build and how to govern AI, with a focus on sales, go-to-market and customer service.
- **Workshop buyers:**
  - The AI Accelerator is a two-day workshop for CEOs and founders, offered by application.
  - Executive AI Fluency is for leadership teams: three hands-on sessions where each leader builds an AI chief of staff.
- **Private AI buyer:** Law firms, accounting firms, mortgage brokers, financial advisors, insurance brokers, notaries, wealth managers and bookkeepers.
- **Business model:** All profiles are B2B. No B2C or B2G targeting was found.

### Company Size Targets

- **Private AI:** Firms of roughly 3 to 25 people. The page says "We set it up for a firm of five."
- **AI advisory:** Small and medium businesses.
- **Product advisory:** Early-stage SaaS companies, based on the "startup founders" wording. No headcount or revenue range is stated.
- **Not targeted:** Enterprise is not named as a target. The older homepage language ("executives and their organizations", board-level AI policy, ISO 42001) hints at larger organizations. Size is Not available for that version.

### Industries

- **Horizontal, SaaS-leaning:** Product and growth advisory is aimed at SaaS startup founders. The AI advisory has no stated vertical.
- **Vertical, regulated professional services:** Private AI is aimed at law firms, accounting firms and other regulated professionals. The full list is in Profiles.
- **Functional focus:** Sales, go-to-market and customer service.

### Geography

- **Base:** Greater Vancouver Metropolitan Area, with the LinkedIn profile listing Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.
- **Target markets:** Not available. The site names no countries or regions served.
- **Inference, unconfirmed:** Private AI is delivered with on-site hardware in the client's office, so it likely favors nearby clients. Remote delivery is not mentioned.

### Use Cases

- **Product advisory:** Turn founder instinct into a product practice, with a clear strategy, an outcome-tied roadmap and evidence customers will pay before building.
- **Growth advisory:** Positioning buyers understand, a product that sells itself where it can, and a sales team equipped where it can't. Then win/loss analysis.
- **AI transformation:** Adopting AI so the business simply runs better, without a visible "big transformation".
- **Private AI:** Staff paste client documents into public chatbots, and that text then sits on a server the firm does not control. The offer is AI models run inside the firm's own firewall so client information never leaves the office. A sample automation is summarizing each new client-folder document and flagging dates and deadlines.
- **AI policy:** The free generator produces a one-page AI use policy, approved tools list, vendor checklist and team rollout.
- **Sales enablement:** Turn positioning into a playbook, battlecards and call plans reps will use.
- **Executive AI fluency:** An AI chief of staff that knows priorities, projects and people and opens each session with a brief.
- **Older homepage version, same themes:** Sales teams drowning in admin, slow marketing content and manual, stale competitive intelligence. Boards asking about AI policy while teams use unreviewed tools.
- **Disqualifiers (Private AI):** Buyers who want AI acting with no human review, who keep all client data in a cloud system they are happy to use AI inside, or who will not name a system owner.

### Clients

- **Named clients or case studies:** Not available. None appear on the homepage or the Private AI page.
- **Founder credibility, not client proof:** Sam was VP of Product at Galvanize, which scaled to a $1B exit, and Chief Product & Technology Officer at Boast AI.
- **Gap to fix:** The site claims "Tools built from real engagements" but shows no engagement or outcome. Adding even anonymized cases per segment would strengthen it.

### Positioning Observations

- **Too many segments:** The site serves four buyer groups: SaaS founders, revenue leaders, SMB owners and regulated small firms. For a solo operator this is broad and likely dilutes the message.
- **Sharpest segment:** Private AI for small regulated professional firms is the most specific. It has a named size band (3 to 25), a clear pain, a clear disqualifier list and a defined timeline (about two months).
- **Free tools as lead generation:** The AI Chief of Staff, AI Use Policy Generator and Sales Enablement Automation are marked free. The Private AI page links the free policy generator as an entry point.
- **Assumption:** Because the profile gives no "what they sell" or competitors, everything above comes from the public website. Confirm which segment is the real revenue priority.

## Strengths

**Scope and basis:** This covers Acme Advisory, a one-person advisory practice run by Sam Rivera. The company profile gives no product description and no named competitors. Everything below comes from the public website and LinkedIn. Claims are self-reported by Acme Advisory and not independently verified. No customer names, revenue, client counts, testimonials, partnerships or certifications were found. Those are marked "Not available".

**Data caveat:** Two versions of the homepage appeared in research.
- The newer version, dated © 2026, positions Acme Advisory as advisory, products and workshops for product, growth and AI.
- The older indexed version positions it as an AI consulting practice helping executives and their organizations lead AI transformation, with an ISO 42001 focus.
- I treated the newer version as current. The change in messaging is itself a finding (see Strategic).

### Product

- **Three service lines, not one product.** The current site offers Advisory (Product, Growth, AI), Products and Workshops.
- **Advisory scope is broad.**
  - Product: turning founder instinct into a product practice the team can run without the founder.
  - Growth: positioning, product-led growth, sales enablement, then win/loss analysis.
  - AI: AI transformation for small and medium businesses.
- **Tools built from real engagements.** The product line includes 10x Employee (an AI operating system), Private AI, AI Chief of Staff, AI Use Policy Generator and Sales Enablement Automation.
  - Private AI runs inside the client's office, so client data stays there. This is a clear privacy-led differentiator.
  - AI Chief of Staff, AI Use Policy Generator and Sales Enablement Automation are marked Free, which works as low-friction lead generation.
- **Workshops are hands-on.** The AI Accelerator is a two-day session for CEOs and founders that ends with a practical AI roadmap. Executive AI Fluency is three sessions where each leader builds an AI chief of staff. Dates are "to be announced".
- **Builder credibility.** The founder still builds AI agents himself. This supports the claim that the tools are real and not slideware.
- **Gaps:** Technical architecture, quality metrics, usage numbers and outcome data are Not available.

### Market

- **Brand recognition:** Low and unmeasured. Search for "Acme Advisory" returned the company site and the founder's LinkedIn profile, and otherwise unrelated results. No press, analyst coverage or reviews were found. Search volume and rankings are Not available.
- **Founder-led visibility.** The founder's LinkedIn shows 500+ connections. He presented the morning keynote at ProductCamp Vancouver. This is a small but real speaking credential.
- **Owned audience.** The site links a newsletter at inhouse.build. Subscriber numbers are Not available.
- **Market sizing and share:** Not available. This is a niche advisory practice with no measurable share.
- **Partnerships:** None found.
- **Customers and case studies:** None named on the pages reviewed. The site says its tools are "built from real engagements", but it does not name the clients.
- **Timely topic.** The founder writes about a trend he is researching: mid-market executives cancelling SaaS subscriptions and building AI capabilities in-house. This is an unverified observation, but it shows he is tracking a live buyer shift.
- **Local base:** Greater Vancouver. This gives a local network and Canadian-market relevance, but no local-market claims are made on the site.

### Operational

- **Capacity: one person.** The profile says "Just me". This is a strength for speed, low overhead and senior attention on every engagement. It is a limit on scale.
- **Productized delivery.** Free tools, workshops and a 30-minute intro call give a clear path from first touch to paid work. This reduces dependence on custom hours.
- **Reusable assets.** The tools come from client work, so each engagement can improve something reusable. This is an inference from the site's wording, not a confirmed process.
- **Booking is simple.** The site has a "Book a call" link on every page.
- **Customer support, SLAs, delivery track record and utilization:** Not available.

### Strategic

- **Founder pedigree.** Sam Rivera has 25 years in business software. He was VP of Product at Galvanize, which the site says scaled to a $1B exit. He was Chief Product & Technology Officer at Boast AI. The older site version says 20 years. The years of experience are inconsistent across pages and should be fixed. The $1B exit claim is self-reported and was not independently verified.
- **Operator, not theorist.** The tagline is "Hands-on advice from someone who has run the function".
- **Focused point of view.** The site argues AI has dropped the cost of building and raised the risk of the "build trap". This is a clear, current thesis.
- **Target buyers:** executive teams, with a focus on sales, go-to-market and customer service, plus SaaS founders and SMBs.
- **Weakness to fix:** Positioning drifted between two versions.
  - Older: executive AI strategy, governance and ISO 42001.
  - Newer: product, growth and AI for founders and revenue leaders.
  - Three buyer groups and three service areas in one page dilute the message.
- **Vision:** The newer headline is "Human Intelligence in the age of AI".
- **Financial position:** Not available. Pricing, revenue and funding are not published.

### Moats

Honest assessment: no structural moats exist yet. The defensible assets are personal and earned, not systemic.

- **Founder track record (strongest).** The Galvanize and Boast AI experience is hard for a new consultant to copy. It does not scale beyond one person.
- **Productized, free tools as an entry point.** The tools are built from client work. They are easy for competitors to imitate, so they are a differentiator and not a moat.
- **Privacy-first Private AI offer.** Keeping client data inside the client's office is a useful wedge for regulated or cautious SMBs. Technical depth and adoption are Not available.
- **Product plus go-to-market plus AI under one practitioner.** Few small advisors combine product management, positioning and AI delivery. This claim comes from the site's offer set, not from competitor research, because no competitors were provided.
- **ISO 42001 expertise (older site version only).** ISO 42001 is the international standard for AI Management Systems. Larger firms already sell this service, including BSI and Fractional CISO. Whether Acme Advisory is certified or accredited to deliver it is Not available. It is not a moat as written.
- **Not moats:** brand, network effects, proprietary data, switching costs, patents and scale. None were found.

### Recommended actions for positioning

1. Pick one primary buyer and one lead offer. Retire or demote the others.
2. Publish at least two named or anonymized case studies with outcomes. Strengths are currently asserted, not proven.
3. Make the founder's credentials consistent across the site (25 versus 20 years).
4. Lead with Private AI and the free tools as proof of building skill, if AI remains the headline.
5. Run a competitor review next. No competitors were provided, so relative strengths could not be assessed.

## Weaknesses

**Scope and assumptions**
- Subject: Acme Advisory (https://acme-advisory.example), a one-person practice run by Sam Rivera. The profile gives no product description and no named competitors.
- The weaknesses below are inferred from public pages and the structure of the market. They are not drawn from customer data.
- Not available: reviews, case studies, testimonials, pricing, revenue and customer counts. I found none for Acme Advisory in public sources.
- Search results for "Acme Advisory" were mostly unrelated (Parallel 9, Parallels, and similar). Search noise is itself a brand weakness.

### Product Gaps

- **Offer is broad and unfocused.** The current site lists three advisory lines:
  - Product management for SaaS startup founders, PLG and GTM strategy for revenue leaders, and AI transformation for small and medium businesses.
  - It also lists five products and two workshops.
  - One person is delivering all of it. There is no single, clear thing to buy.
- **Productized tools look thin and mostly free.**
  - The AI Chief of Staff, AI Use Policy Generator and Sales Enablement Automation are marked "Free".
  - The 10x Employee and Private AI products have no pricing or proof on the homepage.
  - Free tools raise awareness, but there is no visible paid path.
- **Workshops are not yet scheduled.** The AI Accelerator is by application, with dates to be announced. That limits near-term revenue and gives buyers no clear next step.
- **Compliance claims carry a capability gap.** An earlier version of the site promised help to achieve ISO 42001 certification.
  - Certification is a paid audit by an accredited, independent certification body.
  - A solo advisor can prepare a client but cannot certify. The wording should say so.
  - I found no ISO 42001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor credential for Acme Advisory. Buyers are advised to look for formal study of ISO 42001 itself, such as a Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor course.

### Market Challenges

- **Low brand awareness.**
  - A search for the brand name returned no review sites or analyst coverage.
  - The LinkedIn profile shows 3K followers. That is a modest audience for an enterprise-facing advisory practice.
- **Name is hard to find and hard to explain.** "Acme Advisory" collides with unrelated results. The meaning of the name is not explained in the hero copy, and the earlier site used "Define Your North" and "79°N, Svalbard".
- **Inconsistent positioning across public pages.** The same company is described in several ways:
  - An AI consulting practice helping executives lead AI transformation.
  - A firm helping product and revenue leaders define and execute product, growth and AI strategy.
  - An advisory practice for B2B SaaS companies.
  - A consulting practice focused on applying AI to revenue, governance and operations.
  - Audiences shift between executives, SaaS founders, revenue leaders and SMBs. Buyers cannot tell who it is for.
- **Crowded, commoditized category.** AI strategy and ISO 42001 consulting is served by management-system consultancies, AI governance specialists, big firms, software vendors and other solo practitioners. Solo practitioners are strong on price and flexibility but thin on capacity and continuity. Named competitors were not provided, so a direct comparison is not available.
- **Messaging risk on core thesis.** Sam's own writing argues that building software now takes one person and AI tools, and an $80,000-a-year workflow tool can be rebuilt in-house for a fraction of that cost. The same logic can be turned on advisory: clients may build AI capability themselves.
- **Stale third-party profiles.** Crunchbase lists him as Chief Product Officer at Boast and a former Principal at PositioningHQ. It does not mention Acme Advisory.

### Operational Issues

- **Single point of failure.** The company is "Just me". Sales, delivery, content, tooling and support all depend on one person. Illness, a large engagement or a busy quarter stalls everything else.
- **Capacity conflicts with the product-plus-services model.** Advisory work, workshops, a newsletter, a Maven cohort and several tools all draw on the same founder time.
- **No visible delivery proof or support model.** The site shows no case studies, customer logos, testimonials or service terms. The only call to action is a 30-minute intro call. That puts the full sales burden on live conversations.
- **Pricing opacity.** No prices for advisory, workshops or paid products were found. Buyers cannot self-qualify, and it is hard to tell paid offers from free ones.
- **Several domains and brands to maintain.** The ecosystem includes PositioningHQ, a Acme Advisory offering, plus the newsletter site inhouse.build and the main site. Each splits attention and SEO authority.

### Strategic Risks

- **Founder-brand dependency.** The credibility case rests on one résumé. The site says Sam has spent 25 years building business software companies and helped scale Galvanize to a $1B exit. The practice has no independent track record yet. Years of experience are also stated differently across pages, as 20 and as 25.
- **Conflict-of-interest exposure in compliance work.** Independence rules matter in ISO 42001. A certification body may not consult on the system it certifies, so the firm that builds the system cannot certify it. Acme Advisory must stay clearly on the advisory side, and its messaging should say so.
- **Regulatory and standards accuracy risk.** An advisor who claims ISO 42001 makes a client compliant with the EU AI Act is wrong on a point that matters, because certification does not give a presumption of conformity. Overclaiming could damage trust.
- **Timing and hype risk.** The homepage argues that "2026 is everyone else's turn" to master AI. Urgency-led messaging weakens quickly as AI advisory firms multiply and buyers grow skeptical.
- **Financial constraints.** Funding, revenue and runway are not available. A solo practice with several free offers has limited room to invest in marketing, credentials or partners.
- **Platform dependency.** Several offers rely on third-party AI platforms. PositioningHQ's tagline is "Claude changes that, and more," and it is run through a Maven cohort. Changes to Anthropic or Maven terms, pricing or features would directly affect the offer.

### Customer Complaints

- **No customer reviews found.** I found no G2, Capterra, Clutch, Google or testimonial content for Acme Advisory. Customer complaints are Not available.
- **Unrelated results to ignore.** A Capterra listing named "Parallel" is a different company, a KYC and forms tool. It is not Acme Advisory and should not be used as evidence.
- **Likely pain points to test.** These are hypotheses based on how buyers evaluate solo advisors. They are not observed complaints.
  - Unclear scope and deliverables.
  - Availability and continuity if the founder is busy.
  - No proof of results for AI ROI.
  - Pricing that is unclear before a call.
  - Doubt that a solo practice can run a full ISO 42001 program.
- **Next step:** interview 5 to 10 past clients, workshop attendees and free-tool users. Capture quotes and permission to publish them.

## Competitive Analysis

**Selection basis:** Paul Okhrem is the most direct competitor in the four profiles provided. He is a solo, named senior operator selling AI strategy, governance, ISO 42001 readiness and executive workshops to CEOs and boards. That is the closest match to Acme Advisory's one-senior-advisor model. Deloitte competes on brand and scale. TechCXO competes on bench and model. Accorian covers only the compliance slice. The company profile lists no named competitors and leaves "What they sell" blank, so I assumed Acme Advisory is a solo AI consulting practice (AI strategy, governance, ISO 42001, AI sales enablement), as described in memory/research/competitors.md. No web access was used. Everything below comes from the provided documents.

### Executive Summary
Paul Okhrem is a Prague-based solo AI consultant and fractional Chief AI Officer (CAIO). He sells to mid-market and enterprise CEOs and boards, with clients in the US, UK, EU and Middle East. He wins on one named senior operator, published fees, a stated record of running AI inside two companies he leads (Elogic Commerce and Uvik Software), and a search-led content engine. He is vulnerable on price floor (USD 80,000 minimum), a two-client capacity cap, a 30-hours-per-month seat, no named AI client references from his own consulting, and related-party conflicts.

### Strategy

#### Positioning
- **Hero message:** "Paul Okhrem: AI transformation consultant and fractional CAIO" (homepage H1, checked 16 Oct 2026; page updated 7 Oct 2026).
- **Pain point claimed:** AI strategy, operating change, governance and implementation decisions for CEOs and boards. The typical case is AI pilots with no executive owner for priorities, funding and risk.
- **Category claimed:** Fractional CAIO and AI transformation consulting. An older /compare page claimed a narrower category: "decision leverage above strategy."
- **Messaging shift (dates not found, only relative age):**
  - Older: "AI decision consultant" and "Not advice. Decision leverage." Now: "AI transformation consultant."
  - Price floor dropped from USD 1,000/hour, 100-hour minimum, USD 100,000 floor to 80-hour minimum and USD 80,000 floor. Some third-party pages still show the old terms.
  - Tone is more cautious. Pages now say the company results shown belong to Elogic Commerce, not to his independent consulting.
- **Target:** Mid-market and enterprise. Industry pages cover financial services, private equity, healthcare and pharma, ecommerce and retail, and technology and software. A named use case is a PE-backed company before a board review.

#### Pricing and packaging
- **Model:** Published, hourly plus retainer. No free tier.
- **Consulting:** USD 1,000/hour, 80-hour minimum, USD 80,000 floor.
- **Fractional CAIO seat:** USD 30,000/month, six-month minimum, USD 180,000 minimum total. About one day per week, up to 30 hours/month.
- **Workshops:** USD 50,000 or more (contact form).
- **Extras:** Engineering, software and external specialists are billed separately unless explicitly included.
- **Funnel entry:** A free readiness assessment.
- **Comparison to Acme Advisory:** Not available. Acme Advisory's pricing was not provided.

#### Market sentiment
- **Strengths cited:** No independent customer reviews found. Praise appears only on ties-to-him or unclear-ownership sites.
  - Uvik's "Best Fractional CAIO" guide ranks him #1. He is a founder of Uvik, so this is a disclosed commercial relationship.
  - best-ai-consultants-in-the-world.com praises his "operator credibility, production-AI practice, pricing transparency." Ownership is unverified.
- **Weaknesses cited:** No third-party complaints found. His own pages concede he is not a fit for low-cost developers, a large delivery bench, or work below the USD 80,000 floor.

#### Go-to-market
- **Main channel:** Search and AI-answer SEO. Content includes buyer guides, "best AI consultants" lists, statistics pages and free templates. His contact form asks if leads came from Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude or Gemini. He also sells GEO and AEO consulting.
- **Self-ranking content:** His /compare page sets him against Allie K. Miller, Cassie Kozyrkov, Andrew Ng and others, plus Big Four and MBB firms. He discloses it as a first-party comparison.
- **Sales motion:** Inbound only. A private brief gets a reply within two business days: yes, questions, or a no with a referral. Scope and terms are agreed in writing first.
- **Credibility signals:** Forbes Technology Council member (the site notes this is not an endorsement). LinkedIn is linked. Events and partner channels: not found.

### Features

| Offer | What it covers | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Fractional CAIO seat | Part-time executive ownership of AI: strategy, governance, vendor decisions, board reporting, under a written mandate | USD 30,000/month, six-month minimum. Up to 30 hours/month. Capped at two concurrent clients. |
| Scoped AI consulting | One bounded decision, defended. First paid option is the AI Growth Readiness Audit | USD 80,000 for 80 hours over six weeks |
| Agentic AI advisory | Autonomy, permissions and production acceptance for AI agents | No pricing found |
| AI governance and ISO 42001 readiness | Defined scope, owners and gap list before an audit | He does not issue certificates. Certification is a separate decision by an independent body. |
| Board advisory and executive workshops | Governance-level review of AI and technology decisions. Works a real decision with the leadership team | Workshops from USD 50,000 |

- **Recent launches or "coming soon":** Not found. The only dated change is the homepage update (7 Oct 2026) and the price floor reduction.
- **Not offered:** Engineering and build capacity. Engineering stays with the client's team or an implementation partner.
- **Overlap warning:** His nav also lists AI SEO, marketing, revenue, fractional CTO and CIO. I could not verify how this compares with Acme Advisory's AI sales enablement offer.

### SWOT

**Strengths**
- One named senior operator who delivers the work personally.
- Published fees and terms, which lower buyer friction and build trust.
- A claimed record of running AI inside two companies he leads. Results shown belong to Elogic.
- Honest scope limits, such as no certificates and no build work.
- A search and AI-answer content engine that places him on shortlists.
- Specific industry pages for financial services, PE, healthcare, ecommerce and tech.

**Weaknesses**
- Capacity: two concurrent fractional clients.
- High entry cost: USD 180,000 minimum for the seat, USD 80,000 floor for consulting. Smaller buyers are turned away.
- The seat is up to 30 hours/month and does not replace a full-time executive.
- No named AI client references from his own consulting. His site says company roles do not prove an undisclosed client outcome.
- Related-party risk: he leads Elogic and Uvik, which could implement what he recommends.
- Inconsistent claims across pages (100-hour and USD 100,000 older terms versus USD 80,000 now).
- Sprawling offer (AI SEO, marketing, revenue, fractional CTO and CIO) dilutes the CAIO message.
- No build capacity.

**Opportunities (for Acme Advisory)**
- Buyers below his USD 80,000 floor or unwilling to commit six months.
- Buyers who want a bounded engagement, not a seat.
- Buyers who need hands-on adoption and change work with staff. His pages stress decisions, governance and board reporting.
- Buyers who want advice with no implementation stake. He has a disclosed one.
- Verifiable named client proof, if Acme Advisory has it. He has none from consulting.

**Threats**
- His content ranks himself first and shapes AI-answer shortlists. Buyers may meet him before Acme Advisory.
- His floor already fell once. Further cuts would pull him toward Acme Advisory's price band.
- His ISO 42001 readiness page competes directly with Acme Advisory's governance work.
- He openly compares himself with Big Four firms, which strengthens his "senior operator over big bench" story.

### Sales Tactics

#### Trap questions to put to the buyer
Frame these as evaluation criteria. Do not attack him by name.
1. "Who does the work week to week, and how many hours a month will you actually get?" (Seat is up to 30 hours/month, about one day a week.)
2. "What is the total minimum commitment, and what is excluded?" (USD 180,000 for the seat. Engineering and specialists are extra.)
3. "Can you speak with a named client whose AI result came from the advisor's own consulting?" (His site says case results are Elogic's. Named AI client references: not found.)
4. "If the advisor leads a company that builds software, who benefits from the recommendation?" (Elogic and Uvik.)
5. "What happens if the advisor is full?" (Two-client cap.)
6. "Who handles adoption, training and staff change once the strategy is set?" (His pages centre on decisions, governance and board reporting.)
7. "Do you need certification? Who issues it?" (He does not issue certificates. Neither can an advisor who is not an accredited body, so ask Acme Advisory to confirm its own position.)

#### Talking points
- **Lead with fit, not size.** If the buyer is below USD 80,000 or does not want six months, he declines the work himself. Position Acme Advisory as the option sized for that buyer. Confirm Acme Advisory's own price and terms before using this.
- **Independence.** If Acme Advisory has no implementation or affiliated vendor stake, say so plainly. It is a clean contrast to his Elogic and Uvik roles.
- **Proof.** Offer named references and outcome evidence from Acme Advisory's own client work, if available. Not available in the documents provided.
- **Do not claim "named senior person" as a unique edge.** He also sells that. The competitors file flags this edge as an inference.
- **Do not attack his transparency.** Published fees are a real strength. Compete on fit and scope, not on openness.

#### Objections to expect
- "He publishes his rates and you don't." Response: publish Acme Advisory's engagement terms, or give a clear price range early.
- "He has run AI in his own companies." Response: ask which results are his consulting and which are Elogic's, as his own pages say.
- "He is on a Forbes council and ranks first in guides." Response: the council is not an endorsement by his own site's note, and the top rankings are first-party or tied to Uvik.

#### Gaps
- Acme Advisory pricing, offer detail, client proof and win/loss history: not available.
- Independent buyer reviews of Paul Okhrem: not found.
- Messaging history over the last 12 months: only relative dates available.

## Market Overview

*Basis: public website, LinkedIn and third-party research. The profile gives no product description or named competitors, so the offer is taken from the website and the competitor set is inferred.*

### Who They Are
- **Acme Advisory** is a one-person advisory, tools and workshops business run by **Sam Rivera**. It is likely based in Greater Vancouver, Canada, though the site does not say so.
- **Headline:** "Human Intelligence in the age of AI."
- **Founder background:** about 25 years in business software. He was VP of Product at Galvanize (self-reported $1B exit) and Chief Product & Technology Officer at Boast AI. The site also says 20 years in places.
- **Founding date, revenue, funding and customer count:** Not available.

### What They Do
- **Advisory:**
  - Product management for SaaS founders.
  - Product-led growth and go-to-market for revenue leaders.
  - AI transformation for small and medium businesses.
- **Products:**
  - 10x Employee, an AI operating system built on plain files the client owns.
  - Private AI, models run inside the client's office for regulated firms of about 3 to 25 people.
  - Three free tools: AI Chief of Staff, AI Use Policy Generator and PositioningHQ.
- **Workshops:** AI Accelerator (2 days, by application, dates to be announced) and Executive AI Fluency (3 sessions).
- **Claimed edge:** "Hands-on advice from someone who has run the function."
- **Pricing:** mostly unpublished.

### Market Position
- **Segment:** AI consulting and advisory, with adjacent AI governance.
- **Market size:**
  - Analyst estimates put AI consulting at roughly **$5B to $11B in 2025**.
  - Growth forecasts run about **17% to 26% a year**.
  - Definitions differ by source, so treat these as estimates.
  - Acme Advisory's serviceable market: Not available.
- **Standing:** emerging niche player with low, unmeasured brand awareness. Searches for the name return unrelated companies.
- **Messaging shift:**
  - Earlier site: executive AI strategy, governance and ISO 42001, headline "Define Your North."
  - Current site: product, growth and AI for founders and revenue leaders.
  - The timing of the change is not dated.

### Strengths
- **Operator credibility:** a real product executive who says he still builds AI agents.
- **Owned, model-agnostic design:** clients keep their data in plain files and can swap AI models.
- **Privacy-first Private AI:** the sharpest offer, with a named buyer, size band, timeline and disqualifiers.
- **Free tools** work as low-friction lead generation.
- **Timely point of view:** the "build trap" and the shift to building in-house.
- **Simple path to paid work:** a booking link to an intro call.

### Weaknesses
- **Offer sprawl:** three advisory lines, five products and two workshops, all delivered by one person. There is no single lead offer.
- **Audience drift:** the homepage speaks to product and revenue leaders, while most product pages speak to CEOs, owners and regulated firms.
- **Thin proof:**
  - There are no case studies, customer logos or measured outcomes.
  - The research steps disagree on testimonials: one found two named quotes, others found none.
- **Founder dependency:** all sales, delivery and content rest on one person.
- **Pricing opacity** and workshops without dates.
- **Inconsistent claims:** founder tenure, and one product that carries two names (Sales Enablement Automation and PositioningHQ).
- **No structural moats.** The founder's track record is the only hard-to-copy asset, and it does not scale.

### Competitive Landscape
No competitors were named by the founder. The set below is inferred from the category and should be confirmed against real deals.

| Tier | Examples | Wins on | Acme Advisory's angle |
|---|---|---|---|
| Strategy houses | McKinsey QuantumBlack, BCG X, Bain Vector | Board-level brand and scale | Speed and price, with senior attention |
| Big Four and integrators | Deloitte, PwC, EY, KPMG, Accenture, IBM | Governance, controls, scale | Smaller, hands-on engagements |
| Boutiques and fractional | Tribe AI, Addepto, AY Automate and others | Build and engineering depth | Product, positioning and adoption |
| Solo operators | Paul Okhrem | Named senior operator, published fees, SEO | Fit for smaller buyers |
| Alternatives | AI governance software, internal teams, free chief-of-staff tools | Low cost or in-house control | Not stated |

- **Closest rival: Paul Okhrem**, a solo fractional Chief AI Officer.
  - **His fees:** consulting from USD 80,000 and a fractional seat at USD 30,000 a month, with a six-month minimum.
  - **His limits:** a two-client cap, no named AI client references and ties to companies that implement software.
  - **Opening for Acme Advisory:** buyers below his price floor, or buyers who want independent, bounded work.
- **Messaging crowding:** most competitors use generic "AI strategy and transformation" language.

### Key Takeaways
1. **Choose one lead offer and one primary buyer.** Private AI for small regulated firms is the most defined candidate. The founder must confirm which offer drives revenue.
2. **Add proof.** Even anonymized case studies with outcomes would help.
3. **Publish price ranges** and fix the inconsistent claims.
4. **Avoid certification overclaims.** An advisor can prepare a client for ISO 42001 but cannot certify one.
